newsitem.title: GERMANY: German tax talks fail - Waigel.
newsitem.headline: German tax talks fail - Waigel.

text.p: Negotiations between the German coalition government and the opposition Social Democrats (SPD) to seek a compromise on tax reforms have failed, Finance Minister Theo Waigel said on Wednesday.
Speaking after a short meeting between the two sides, Waigel said the SPD had refused to back coalition plans to cut taxes and reform state pensions.
"The SPD wants to cut occupational insurance charges by simply redistributing wealth," Waigel told reporters after the talks, which lasted just over an hour.

Waigel vowed to press on with the coalition's legislative agenda, which foresees passing a package of 30 billion marks in tax cuts through the Bundestag lower house of parliament before the summer recess.

The SPD would then block the measures through its majority in the Bundesrat upper house, meaning that ways out of the standoff would have to be sought through parliament's mediation process some time in the autumn.
"The government is absolutely determined to push ahead with its policies. We cannot come to a standstill," he said.
